summary: The note surveys how blockchain startups are disrupting industries beyond cryptocurrency, including finance, supply chain, healthcare, energy, and intellectual property. It profiles specific startups, compares their agility with tech giants, and covers the surge in venture funding. It closes by noting regulatory uncertainty and growing dialogue between startups and regulators.
one_line: Blockchain startups are challenging established players in finance, supply chains, healthcare, energy and IP, backed by rising investment but facing regulatory uncertainty.
key_facts: Blockchain began on January 3, 2009, when the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto mined the first block of bitcoins.
A Global Blockchain Business Council report published September 15, 2023 cites decentralization, immutability, and transparency as blockchain's advantages over centralized systems.
ProxiSecure, a fintech startup founded December 1, 2023 by Maria Gomez, offers secure peer-to-peer lending without traditional banking infrastructure.
At the Blockchain Accelerate Conference on February 20, 2024, Maria Gomez said blockchain is "not here to abolish banks, but to improve the way people interact with their finances."
ChainTrack, founded November 10, 2023 by logistics analyst James Choi, uses blockchain to create tamper-proof shipment records and combat counterfeit goods.
Healthchain, established January 5, 2024 by medical professionals and blockchain experts, lets patients control their medical data securely.
PowerLedger, launched September 30, 2023 by engineers Anna Liu and Raphael Martins, enables peer-to-peer trading of excess renewable energy without the traditional grid.
CreatiWise, founded October 12, 2023 and led by Eleanor Hughes, lets creators register, track, and manage intellectual property and sell different degrees of usage rights.
Blockchain startups thrive on agility and niche specialization, while giants like Google, Amazon, and Facebook are encumbered by legacy systems and massive scale.
A Blockchain Investment Trends report released September 25, 2023 says blockchain startup funding hit unprecedented levels, with a 150% increase in investment after the second quarter of 2024.
Sentinel Chain closed a $30 million Series A round on October 16, 2023, and offers blockchain-based land titling for people in developing countries without formal land documentation.
Lack of a tailored legal framework is a major hurdle for blockchain startups.
The International Blockchain Association held a regulator-startup roundtable on September 5, 2024, one of several such forums.
